payload.consequence: A superseded brief and a reversed label pair remain in the public tracker on #10. The reversal surfaced on a user follow-up question about the state assignment, not at any skill-prescribed step; the skill's verification and recommendation steps ran and passed with the framing that was later retracted, so whether any prescribed step would have caught it is undetermined. No downstream reliance occurred: #10 was never labeled ready-for-agent while the retracted brief stood alone.
payload.expected: Triage of one issue reaches one terminal state assignment with one brief posted.
payload.observed: #10 was assigned ready-for-human with a brief, then reassessed within the same session to ready-for-agent with a second brief explicitly superseding the first, and a second issue (#11) was created to carry the other half of the work.
payload.run_condition: One issue triaged against a five-document constitution and a private skill set; several verification batches ran before the first recommendation; the problem surfaced late, after the first brief was posted and labeled, and was caught by user prompting rather than by a gate.

payload.consequence: The brief was posted and complies with the rule. Whether the descriptive naming is sufficient is not determinable from this session: the check that would show it is an implementing agent resolving those descriptions to the actual documents, and that has not run. No rework occurred within this session.
payload.expected: Per the skill's agent-brief reference, a ready-for-agent brief describes behaviour, interfaces and acceptance criteria and does not name file paths or line numbers, so it stays valid while the codebase moves under it.
payload.observed: The ratified change's subject matter was specific documents — an existing ADR to amend in place, a shipped skill package's reference document, and that document's review-report template — where each document's identity is the substance of the work rather than an incidental location. Every mention required deciding case by case whether naming it breached the no-paths rule, and each was ultimately written as a description instead of a name.
payload.run_condition: Single-issue triage run end to end in one long session — context gathering, claim verification with three CLI reproductions against a locally built binary, a four-fork grilling, then outcome application. The tension surfaced late, at the final outcome step while drafting the agent brief, and was noticed during drafting rather than caught by any gate.
payload.workaround_taken: Named each affected document by its role and by the decision it records rather than by path.

payload.consequence: The recommendation the maintainer received rested on verified premises and needed no retraction, and the first direction was given on that basis. What the documented order would have cost was not incurred and is therefore undetermined — no turn in this session presented a recommendation ahead of verification.
payload.expected: Following the documented step order, the maintainer receives the category and state recommendation at step 2 and gives direction, and the reporter's claim is verified at step 3, before any grilling.
payload.observed: The step-2 recommendation depends on the verification that step 3 performs. The issue's central premise — that no artifact before the irreversible write names what an instrument-limited close retires — did not hold, and only the step-3 reproduction established that. The session ran the verification before drafting the step-2 recommendation, inverting the documented order; the inversion was not noted at the time and is visible only on review of the completed session.
payload.run_condition: One top-level session of roughly forty tool calls; the inversion occurred early, at the first approach to step 2, after reading the issue and the skill's reference docs and before any recommendation was drafted. No gate or check caught it during the run.
payload.workaround_taken: Ran step 3's reproduction before presenting step 2's recommendation, then folded the corrected premises into the recommendation and into the agent brief.

payload.consequence: No rework and no wrong deliverable; the recommendation was sound when first presented because verification was front-loaded. Under the documented order the maintainer would have been asked to direct a close before the surviving gap was known.
payload.expected: The documented step order - gather context, recommend and wait for direction, then verify the claim - produces a sound recommendation at the recommend step.
payload.observed: The recommend step requires stating whether the request is already implemented, but the verification that settles that question is sequenced after the wait for direction. The step-one redundancy search found an existing CI check covering the request, which under the literal order supports recommending wontfix-already-implemented; only verification work belonging to the later step, run against a throwaway clone, showed the existing check misses newly emitted untracked files and that a narrower real gap survived. Step five's outcome branches also contain no case for a stated ask that is already implemented while a narrower gap remains, so a re-scope route was constructed and offered as a choice.
payload.run_condition: One GitHub issue triaged in a single session of roughly twenty tool calls; twelve test suites and one CI workflow inspected plus four installer probes against a throwaway clone; the ordering tension surfaced early, at the first approach to the recommend step, and was caught while assembling that recommendation rather than by any gate in the skill.
payload.workaround_taken: Ran the claim-verification step's work during context gathering, before the documented wait for direction.
